title: Last Date to Stop Auto-Renewal After the Notice Window Grew
scenario_text:
Rosa Telecom manages vendor contract renewals under its Contract Renewal Policy, which sets how much advance notice is needed to prevent automatic renewal.

Version 1 (in effect through 2024-10-31): "To prevent automatic renewal, written non-renewal notice must be delivered at least 60 days before the contract's renewal date."

Version 2 (effective 2024-11-01): "To prevent automatic renewal, written non-renewal notice must be delivered at least 90 days before the renewal date." Version 2 adds a transition clause: "The non-renewal notice window applicable to a contract is determined by its renewal date. Contracts whose renewal date falls on or after January 1, 2025 are subject to the 90-day window. Contracts whose renewal date falls before January 1, 2025 retain the 60-day window."

The contract repository shows vendor agreement VA-1174 (vendor: Summit Fiber): Renewal Date 2025-02-15, Auto-Renewal enabled, Term 12 months. Procurement wants to exit this agreement and not renew. The repository shows no notice has yet been delivered, no amendment altering the notice clause, and a delivery method of written notice to the vendor's contract address on file. The renewal date of 2025-02-15 is confirmed against the executed agreement.

A procurement specialist writes in #vendor-contracts on 2024-11-05: "We're not renewing VA-1174; its renewal date is February 15, 2025. The old policy needed 60 days, so I had December 17 in my head as the deadline to send notice. But the window changed. What's the actual last date we can deliver the non-renewal notice to stop the auto-renewal?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the contract record, determine the last date Rosa Telecom can deliver the non-renewal notice for VA-1174.
question: What is the last date Rosa Telecom can deliver the non-renewal notice for VA-1174?
